steps.title: Graph browser with RFC on the center node
steps.caption: The graph-browser example opens with Reinforcement Focus+Context active on its central Graph browsers node. Yellow halos identify the reinforced center and its five immediate branches; the surrounding graph retains its ordinary connections and forces.

steps.title: Reveal the complete graph
steps.caption: Show whole graph reveals stored nodes beyond the current neighborhood. Expansion, collapse and hiding change the visible graph while retaining the complete graph for editing and export.

steps.title: Graph spacing, canvas zoom and viewing lens
steps.caption: Graph spacing changes node distances. Canvas zoom scales shapes, labels and strokes together. The focus + context slider applies the independent nonlinear viewing lens.

steps.title: User key map
steps.caption: The help dialog and docs/KEYMAP.md share the same implemented command definitions, including graph spacing, canvas zoom, navigation, editing and file shortcuts.

steps.title: Node types and curved relations
steps.caption: The palette page shows all 21 configured Freshmind node types, labeled curved relations, parallel edges and a self-loop. Its YAML editor applies semantic and visual configuration to the existing graph.

steps.title: Open the approved Berry example
steps.caption: Berry is one of the two approved migrated datasets. The native YAML graph retains 21 nodes and 22 relations, annotations and original linked-resource paths.

steps.title: Florentine families
steps.caption: This public example has 15 families and 20 undirected marriage links. Node content contains graph-derived summaries and links to the connected families, with source attribution retained in the document.

steps.title: Edit a multiline node label
steps.caption: F2 opens an inline label editor on the selected node. A draft stays separate from the model until committed; node identity, relations and annotations are retained.

steps.title: Annotations and item details
steps.caption: Ctrl+Enter commits the label. Space or Show details opens the selected node's content in a separate, resizable popup. Internal links navigate to connected nodes; Edit content delegates to the annotation inspector.

steps.title: Save the complete graph as YAML
steps.caption: Ctrl+Shift+S opens the filename dialog. Saving downloads the complete stored graph, including hidden nodes, with optional layout/view state and embedded or companion type configuration.

steps.title: Single-focus comparison: ordinary layout
steps.caption: The synthetic crowded-star fixture uses a fixed center and fixed context anchors. This is the ordinary TouchGraph layout after 250 batches from the saved initial coordinates; RFC is off. Both comparison views use 200% graph spacing and 100% canvas zoom for readability.

steps.title: Single-focus comparison: attraction reinforcement
steps.caption: Reload the identical graph, choose Attraction only and run 250 batches. This earlier preset combines attraction multiplier 3 with angular stiffness 300, without a target-length spring. Soft yellow halos identify the reinforced nodes and relations; semantic graph records remain unchanged.

steps.title: Single-focus comparison: length-constrained tree
steps.caption: The default Tree structure preset combines target focal length 120, radial stiffness 1 and angular stiffness 10000. From the same starting graph and after 250 batches, the focal star is more regular. Both stronger angular constraints and the new length spring contribute. Yellow halos show reinforcement; optional focal-region exclusion is demonstrated separately below.

steps.title: Weighted RFC for horizontally extended labels
steps.caption: The wide-label fixture uses horizontal coordinate weight 0.25 and vertical weight 1. Equal angles are measured in weighted physical coordinates, permitting a wider focal layout while the viewing lens and both zooms stay independent. Ordinary context springs still compete with reinforcement; the metric alone does not guarantee clear space or eliminate label overlaps.

steps.title: Reinforce multiple stored trees
steps.caption: Two saved tree definitions reinforce deeper neighborhoods at the same time. Their context relations remain ordinary graph edges. Stored membership survives YAML export; active RFC centers are temporary view state. Shift+Enter can also add or remove an individual center.

steps.title: Overlapping clusters and their boundaries
steps.caption: RFC can reinforce cyclic clusters as well as trees. These two stored clusters share a member, retain their internal relations and show translucent boundaries. Cluster rigidity controls resistance to deformation; the representative selects the group without becoming a physical anchor.

steps.title: Optional focal-region exclusion
steps.caption: Dashed physical regions show the space reserved around two reinforced structures. Optional exclusion pushes context and non-shared focal nodes away from those regions while shared members remain exempt from their own regions. The forces are soft; pinned nodes and labels can still overlap.

steps.title: Node importance and exact weight values
steps.caption: Node weight scales body and label size within configured limits. Weight 1 keeps normal size and weight 0 remains visible. Optional values make weights explicit when labels differ in length. Size shows importance; yellow halos independently show RFC participation.

steps.title: Combine RFC with structural aggregation
steps.caption: The structural focus + context example combines a viewing lens, RFC and reversible Person/Paper leaf aggregation. Six of thirteen nodes remain visible, with seven aggregated leaves counted under their parents. The shared collaborator stays visible because it connects two semantic neighbors. The complete graph remains intact.

steps.title: Reveal aggregated detail without losing context
steps.caption: Select Group Beta and reveal its leaves to restore detail while retaining the current graph, focal center and lens. Nine nodes are now visible. E also reveals a selected parent's leaves; Reset structural view restores the current neighborhood without deleting semantic data.

steps.title: Browse the approved NIPS dataset
steps.caption: NIPS-FM contains 3,777 nodes and 5,257 relations. Opening it starts with a bounded neighborhood; the full graph remains stored for subsequent navigation and export.

steps.title: Inspect overlapping node labels
steps.caption: The graph-browser example retains RFC on its center node. Point-based layout can leave wide node labels intersecting even when their centers are apart. Label spacing uses the measured visible bodies, including multiline labels and importance scaling.

steps.title: Separate overlapping nodes
steps.caption: Separate overlapping nodes arranges visible bodies with a requested gap and pauses motion. Pinned nodes and the viewing focus stay in place; semantic relations, RFC, hidden nodes and viewing settings are retained. The status reports remaining intersections. Resuming motion or changing the view can introduce new overlaps; relation labels and crossings are separate concerns.

steps.title: Inspect original relation-label positions
steps.caption: With node bodies already separated and motion paused, turn off Avoid relation label overlaps to inspect the original midpoint-and-offset anchors. Relation text can still intersect node bodies or other relation labels. The following view uses these exact node positions and curves.

steps.title: Place relation labels near clear curve positions
steps.caption: Avoid relation label overlaps measures SVG text and tries nearby positions along each curve and its normal. The browser enables this bounded presentation pass by default. It reduces label–node and label–label intersections in this view while retaining every label, node position and curve. Dense views can still overlap; toggling off restores original anchors.
